newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria leads way in a tepid Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria leads way in a tepid Brady market.

text.p: Bulgaria's debt carried on with its bounce on Tuesday in a generally dithering, though well-supported, emerging debt market.

"I don't see much upside. We'll need very good (U.S.) numbers to push this market up...but if we don't see any bad figures, it will go all right to the end of the year," ABN-AMRO trader Marcello Vasquez said.
This week sees U.S. data for producer and consumer prices for November.
Brazil C bonds BR8D14=RR have been meeeting some resistance at 73-1/2 cents in the dollar. They are currently bid at 73-1/8.
Russian Vnesh paper slipped in the morning but MinFins were firmer.
Investors are focusing on how quickly the International Monetary Fund will be prepared to release a delayed loan and chances of the budget passing through the Duma.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said earlier he hoped the 1997 draft budget would pass through its first reading in parliament on December 15.
Bulgaria continued its firmer trend, based on optimism that the government will introduce a currency board and so be assured of an IMF loan it needs to avoid default next year on its debt servicing.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said he hoped parliament would vote on the introduction of a currency board on January 2 and has pledged a package of measures to stabilise the economy.
But a number of analysts are extremly cautious about hailing Bulgaria's prospects yet and question the government's ability to deliver promised reforms.
"If they establish a currency board it would be a step forward. But it's no panacea," Chase Manhattan analyst Robin Hubbard said.
He added it was still unclear whether there was the political concensus to adopt the currency system and protect the crumbling lev.
